note: One line through the science tutorials. The plane is schematic: a picture of the idea, not one measured system. Each station is a different physical system placed on one shared drawing.

x.name: the knob along the line
x.meaning: a second control setting, such as a coupling or an applied field, that moves a system along its edge; dimensionless, schematic

y.name: temperature, scaled
y.meaning: how hard random jiggling pushes against order, relative to the system's own edge; dimensionless, schematic

z.name: nearness to criticality
z.meaning: a normalised reading from 0 (far from any edge) to 1 (at a critical point); no units

track_level_meaning: c is the height the track rides at: a level just below the bead tops, so the track threads every peak and crosses the valleys between them on bridges

stations.title: Ticket hall: why ride?
stations.view: the whole country from above, before you board
stations.phase: the whole surface from above: edges are where behaviour changes

carry.name: poised
carry.gloss: poised: sitting at an edge between two kinds of behaviour instead of falling to one side; the word is used in three different senses, set side by side at the terminus

stations.title: The first edge
stations.phase: one critical point; the ride starts at the spike

carry.name: critical point, order parameter
carry.gloss: critical point: the exact setting at which a system changes its kind of behaviour, and small pushes have large effects; order parameter: a number that is zero on one side of the change and grows on the other, like the pull of a magnet

stations.title: Hall of mirrors
stations.view: every cliff looks the same up close
stations.phase: renormalisation flow to a fixed point: why the exponents repeat
stations.expert_title: The Renormalization Group for the Working Mathematician

carry.name: universality, fixed point
carry.gloss: universality: very different systems share the same numbers near their critical points; fixed point: a state that looks the same after you zoom out, which is why those numbers repeat

stations.title: An edge with no cliff
stations.view: the track runs along a ridge
stations.phase: the Kosterlitz-Thouless line: a line of critical states with no local order parameter

carry.name: BKT, stiffness jump
carry.gloss: BKT (Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless): a change in flat, two-dimensional systems in which tiny whirlpools (vortices), bound in pairs, come apart; stiffness jump: the system's resistance to being twisted drops suddenly to zero at the change

stations.title: The grade changes
stations.phase: the Ashkin-Teller line: the exponents vary continuously along the line

carry.name: Ashkin-Teller, four-spin coupling
carry.gloss: Ashkin-Teller: a model of two magnets sharing one lattice; four-spin coupling: the strength of the link between the two, which moves the system along a whole line of critical points whose numbers change as you go

stations.title: The workshop
stations.phase: the model zoo and the tools: finite-size scaling, the Binder cumulant

carry.name: finite-size scaling
carry.gloss: finite-size scaling: reading the behaviour of an endless system from simulations of several finite sizes, by watching how what you measure changes with size

stations.title: The tunnel
stations.phase: where a line turns first-order: coexistence, two states at once
stations.expert_title: Jumps, Slowing, and the Line They Sit On

carry.name: first-order, coexistence
carry.gloss: first-order: a change with a jump, like ice melting, instead of a smooth critical change; coexistence: both kinds of behaviour present at once, side by side, at the jump

stations.title: Beads on a string
stations.phase: a beaded line: critical points lined up on one line, with real valleys between them; in the fractional quantum Hall effect of a two-dimensional electron gas, the sharp changes between plateaus line up this way, one example among several

carry.name: fractional quantum Hall, filling factor
carry.gloss: fractional quantum Hall effect: in a thin sheet of electrons in a strong magnetic field, the resistance sits on flat steps at certain fractions and changes sharply between them; filling factor: the number that says how full the electrons' allowed energy levels are, which picks out the steps

stations.title: The window that shows the edge coming
stations.view: the window fogs before the edge arrives
stations.phase: what an instrument reads near the line: variance, autocorrelation; why a point detector misreads a line

carry.name: early-warning signal
carry.gloss: early-warning signal: a change in how a system jiggles, such as larger and slower swings, that can appear as it nears a tipping point

stations.title: The instrument
stations.view: what keeps the train on the line
stations.phase: the Criticality Compass, a planned instrument set out in a deposited design note; nothing is yet shown to work

carry.name: Criticality Compass
carry.gloss: Criticality Compass: a planned instrument for telling whether measurements sit near a critical point, along a critical line, or neither; its design note is deposited (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23965603) and nothing is yet shown to work

stations.title: Terminus: the honest ending
stations.view: three doors, one not yet opened
stations.phase: the three senses of poised, the critics, and the strongest independent support
stations.expert_title: The Poised State and Its Critics

carry.name: Poised Realm
carry.gloss: Poised Realm: the newest of the three senses of poised, a proposal that some molecules of life sit at the edge between conducting and insulating, where quantum effects can last long enough to matter
